9.1 Register
WARNING: To prevent impaired ventilation and patient injury, the procedure should be performed under general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation, Electrocardiography (ECG) monitoring, and ventilator alarms.
Registration is the process used to match the airway Live View with the Navigation View. During registration, the system collects apical and basal data for each lung. These apical and basal segments are displayed on the system as four quadrants, which are regional divisions of the Airway Tree (that is, the quadrants are not anatomically divided by lobe).
Follow the steps on the top monitor to perform airway registration.
1. Drive to main carina.
a.
Match the Live View to the Navigation View in centering, depth, and rotation. If the views do not match, adjust the Live View as needed. Adjust centering using the trackball, adjust depth using the scroll wheel, or adjust rotation using the Controller touchscreen.
b. Tap Confirm Main Carina on the Controller touchscreen.
2. If you would like to start video recording, tap Start Video . This button is always accessible from the Quick Tools panel.
3. Start survey by driving into each main bronchus until the right and left indicators are illuminated.
4. Drive into one apical and one basal segment in each lung until the indicator for each quadrant illuminates. The border of the quadrant you are currently in is highlighted.
Note: Use Show Lung Regions to display the separation of the lung into the four quadrants with their associated colors on the Airway Tree (note that these quadrants are not based on lobes).
If the system checks the wrong quadrant, continue to drive to all four apical and basal regions of the lung. If quadrant checks are missing after you have navigated to all four regions, proceed with partial registration. It is not recommended to continue navigating to get all four quadrant checks if apical and basal data has been gathered.
5. Evaluate registration and tap Accept Registration or Redo Registration on the Controller touchscreen.
To evaluate registration, navigate beyond the main carina and evaluate the relationship between the Live View and the Navigation View, especially at carinas proximal to the region of interest. Some discrepancy may occur due to biological motion.
· Redo registration if there is a visual mismatch between the Live View and Navigation View during navigation, or if there is significant patient or system movement.
· Redo registration if the Swivel Connector is undocked from the arm, the arm clutch button is pressed, the System Cart brakes are unlocked, or the Catheter is removed from the system mid-procedure.
9.2 Navigate
After registration is complete, the first planned destination (target and path) automatically appears on screen. The planned pathway to the target appears on the Navigation View, Tree View, and Progress View. It is possible to switch to an alternate target or pathway if one was planned.
Navigation of the Catheter through the airways should be performed in a minimally traumatic manner by attempting to stay in the center of the airways at all times.
To navigate to the target and position the Catheter for biopsy:
1. Use the Controller to drive the Catheter through the planned pathway to the target. Watch the Live View while driving.
2. Once the target is reached, note the message to use fluoroscopic guidance when extending tools past the tip of the Catheter.
3. (Optional) Perform a radial endobronchial ultrasound (R-EBUS) using fluoroscopy to confirm the target location.
a. Position the Catheter for R-EBUS approximately 10 mm proximal to the lesion.
Ensure there is a small gap between the tip of the Catheter and the airway wall to allow the R-EBUS probe to exit the Catheter. If needed, pull back the Vision Probe slightly to visually confirm that the Catheter points to the airway wall.
b. Adjust the fluoroscope to match the optimal fluoro angle on the top monitor.
c. Remove the Vision Probe from the Catheter and keep the Vision Probe out of the way by placing it into the Vision Probe Bag.
d. Perform R-EBUS. If needed, use Fluoro Reference and Articulation Guide with R-EBUS to localize the target (see Biopsy Tab on page 41).
e. If needed, select Move Target to update the target position (see Biopsy Tab on page 41).
f. Re-insert the Vision Probe into the Catheter.
4. Position the Catheter for biopsy.
· Using Navigation View for reference, aim the Catheter as straight as possible toward the center of the target.
· Ensure the target is within striking distance of the needle (approximately 30 mm).
· For endoluminal targets: Position the Catheter tip directly against the target.
· For extra bronchial targets: Position the Catheter tip against the airway wall for stability. If needed, pull the Vision Probe back slightly to visually confirm that the Catheter tip sits directly against the airway wall.
5. Remove the Vision Probe from the Catheter and keep the Vision Probe out of the way by placing it into the Vision Probe bag.
6. For biopsy, adjust the fluoroscope to match the optimal fluoro angle on the top monitor.
9.3 Biopsy Overview
WARNING: To prevent patient injury, do not use excessive force during the insertion or extraction of the Vision Probe, biopsy needle, or bronchoscopic tools through the Catheter tool channel.
WARNING: When a system fault occurs, retract the tool inside the protective sheath immediately to minimize interaction with tissue and prevent patient injury as the Catheter slowly releaxes in response to the fault.
Note: Vibrations from insertion or extraction of the Vision Probe, biopsy needle, or bronchoscopic tools through the Catheter tool channel may result in Catheter sensor interference. When interference is detected, the system transitions the Catheter to passive state. Recover on the Controller touchscreen and reposition the Catheter as needed.
Before Biopsy
Ensure that the fluoroscope or other third-party visualization sources are connected to the System Cart and are functional.
Before Tool Exchange
Before inserting or removing any tool through the Catheter tool channel, check the Bend Radius on the monitor to ensure there is sufficient space to pass the tool through the Catheter tip.
Whereas the Progress View indicates the Catheter bends along the shaft, the Tip Indicator shows the direction the Catheter tip is bent, and the Bend Radius shows the tightest bend on the Catheter (measured in millimeters).
The bend radius must be large enough when passing the following tools:
· Flexision Biopsy Needle : 15 mm or greater
· Third-party tools : 20 mm or greater
· Forceps : 25 mm or greater
For guidance selecting compatible third-party tools, see the third-party tools table in 8.2 Select Compatible Third-Party Biopsy Tools on page 58.
If needed, relax the Catheter before passing a tool as follows:
1. (Optional) Before entering the passive state, place a biopsy marker to mark your biopsy position. After passing the tool, you can return to active mode and re-articulate to the biopsy marker to return to your parked position.
2. Relax the Catheter using either method:
· Articulate the Catheter toward the white arrow on the tip indicator to increase the bend radius.
· Press the Passive button on the Controller to put the Catheter in passive (relaxed) mode.
3. Pass the tool.
CAUTION: If resistance is felt when removing the Vision Probe or tool from the Catheter tool channel, do not continue retracting the device, as this may result in device damage. Remove the Catheter and Vision Probe or tool together.
4. If needed, press the Passive button again to return to active mode.
5. Re-articulate the Catheter to your biopsy position.
After Biopsy Always Evaluate Airway
WARNING: Insert the Vision Probe after biopsy to assess airways for trauma or bleeding to prevent delayed intervention in case of an emergency.
After a biopsy, insert the Vision Probe back in the Catheter to check for bleeding, and to inspect the Catheter liner for damage. If the liner is damaged, replace the Catheter.
9.4 Flexision Needle Biopsy
WARNING: Always inspect the biopsy needle for damage before and during use. A damaged needle can contain loose fragments that may cause toxic reaction if left in the patient.
WARNING: Use fluoroscopic visualization (fluoroscopy) when advancing tools past the tip of the Catheter. Failure to use fluoroscopy during biopsy may result in patient injury.
WARNING: Always reset the needle stop (re-sheath the needle): before removing the biopsy needle from the Catheter tool channel, after preparing the sample, or before transferring the needle between staff. Failure to reset the needle stop during handling or hand-offs may result in infection or injury by needle stick.
WARNING: If you notice damage to the inside of the Catheter during use, replace the Catheter. A damaged Catheter can contain loose fragments that may cause toxic reaction if left in the patient.
CAUTION: Proceed with caution if the biopsy needle is inserted or removed through a Catheter bend radius smaller than 15 mm. Insertion and removal of the biopsy needle should not be performed against increased resistance. Failure to follow instructions may result in Catheter or needle damage.
CAUTION: Exercise caution when inserting the biopsy needle into the Catheter tool channel with the sheath extended. Failure to do so may result in patient injury.
1. Inspect the biopsy needle prior to use. If damaged, dispose and replace the needle.
a. Before use of the needle, confirm the label is legible and is the intended needle size.
b. Before use and between each use, inspect the needle for the following:
· Damage to sheath shaft, sheath tip, needle tube, and needle point (for example, burrs or dull edges at needle point, loose or separated needle, or kinks).
· Foreign matter.
· Friction when extending needle, or inability to fully extend needle (approximately 3 cm).
· Blocked or kinked lumen. Check by flushing with saline.
Ensure needle stop is functioning properly. Proper function is described as:
· When the needle stop is pressed, the needle stop should slide freely.
· When the needle stop is released, the needle stop should be locked.
· Stylet does not extend beyond the tip of the needle (more than 3 mm).
c. Before inserting or reinserting into the Catheter tool channel, confirm the needle is fully retracted and locked within the sheath, the needle sheath home position mark is fully exposed, and the thumbscrew has locked the sheath extension.
2. Insert the biopsy needle through the Catheter tool channel. Secure the needle to the Catheter.
3. Under fluoroscopy, position the sheath for biopsy. Position the sheath so that it extends slightly beyond the Catheter, by loosening the thumbscrew on the needle handle. Approximately ¼ (one-fourth) turn of the thumbscrew allows the sheath to move back and forth.
a. Look for tenting under fluoroscopy (indicated by backward movement of the Catheter).
b. Confirm that the Catheter and sheath are aligned to the target.
c. After placement of the sheath tip, tighten the thumbscrew to lock the sheath position.
WARNING: Confirm the relation of the patient anatomy to the biopsy target (for example, distances to target and anatomy borders) before setting needle stroke length. Setting the incorrect needle stroke length may lead to pneumothorax.
4. While stabilizing the needle handle, set the needle insertion depth using the needle stop up to 3 cm based on the distance to the target and size of the target.
The insertion distance should be based on physician discretion. The estimated distance of the Catheter to the target is shown on the monitor. Consider minimum distance to target as provided by the navigation, sheath extension, and fluoroscopy before choosing a needle extension length.
5. Under fluoroscopy, insert the needle with one jab towards the target.
If needed, check the recommended fluoro arm angle on the monitor and adjust the fluoro arm.
6. Once the needle is inserted, remove the stylet from the back end of the needle while holding the needle in place.
At the physician's discretion, suction can be attached to the needle. For suction, connect the stopcock to the vacuum syringe provided with the needle. With the stopcock closed, pull back vacuum for 5 to 20 mL. Connect the stopcock to the needle and open the valve towards the needle.
Note: Select a vacuum locking syringe and stopcock with standard luer lock connectors (luer fittings compliant with ISO 80369-7) that can suction up to 20 mL.
7. Perform multiple jabs with the needle, per physician discretion.
8. Remove the vacuum syringe and, under fluoroscopy, fully retract the needle into the sheath, and return the needle stop to the home position.
9. If desired, fully retract the sheath and tighten the thumbscrew. If you opt to keep the sheath extended for further passes, exercise caution when re-inserting the needle into the Catheter tool channel.
10. Press the connector key and pull the biopsy needle from the Catheter tool channel.
11. Evaluate airway.
Perform airway evaluation after all the biopsy passes are complete. Insert the Vision Probe into the Catheter to evaluate the biopsy site for any bleeding.
Remove Samples
1. Take the biopsy needle to the back table for retrieving samples.
a. Set the needle insertion limit.
b. With the sheath pointing towards the sample tray, advance the needle.
c. Push the sample out using a syringe filled with air.
The sample can also be pushed out using the stylet, if the sample is stuck in the needle.
2. Use a syringe to inject saline in the needle to collect the remaining sample.
a. Retract the needle and secure the needle stop.
b. Reinsert the stylet into the needle and lock in place. Ensure the needle is not damaged (for example, bent or broken).
Repeat Needle Biopsy
1. To repeat biopsy, insert the needle and repeat the needle biopsy steps to perform another biopsy pass from the same target to collect an appropriate sample size, at the physician's discretion.
2. Perform biopsy passes.
At the physician's discretion, use the biopsy marker feature to indicate multiple biopsy attempts. Use the trackball to articulate to another area of the target to take another biopsy.
Use the orientation guide on the bottom monitor to determine how to move the trackball for the desired Catheter tip articulation. Move the trackball to the right, left, up, or down like a clock. For example, in the image below, to articulate the Catheter tip in the cranial direction, move the trackball towards 7 o'clock.
The Endoluminal Compass is a fixed sphere with directional indicators that display in the Navigation View around the orientation guide. The directional indicators represent anatomical headings that are determined by the pre-procedure CT scan. The Endoluminal Compass is set to visible by default.
Medial and lateral indicators on the Endoluminal Compass and the orientation guide change based on the location of the Catheter.
3. Remove samples from the needle (see Remove Samples on page 82).
9.5 Compatible Third-Party Tool Use
For third-party tool selection guidance, see 8.2 Select Compatible Third-Party Biopsy Tools on page 58.
Note: Do not advance forceps through the Catheter tool channel if the bend radius is smaller than 25 mm. Do not advance any other third-party tools if the bend radius is smaller than 20 mm.
Note: The rotational orientation of third-party tools is not controlled through the Catheter tool channel. Rotation may affect insertion and retraction through the Catheter.
1. Insert compatible third-party tools through the Catheter tool channel.
a. Ensure that the Catheter bend radius is greater than 25 mm if inserting forceps or greater than 20 mm if inserting any other third-party tools.
b. Once the device is inserted, the Catheter can be articulated to achieve a tighter bend radius, if needed.
2. Deploy the tool to retrieve the sample of the target tissue under fluoroscopy.
3. Remove the tool and evaluate the airway. Insert the Vision Probe into the Catheter to evaluate the biopsy site for bleeding.
Forceps
WARNING: Failure to properly insert or remove forceps through the Catheter tool channel may damage the forceps, resulting in procedure delay or foreign body in the patient.
Note: The Catheter must be in passive mode prior to retracting biopsy forceps.
Note: Slowly insert and retract biopsy forceps through the Catheter tool channel. Quickly inserting and retracting may result in Catheter sensor interference. When interference is detected, the system transitions the Catheter to passive state. Recover on the Controller touchscreen and reposition the Catheter as needed.
1. Press the Passive
button on the Controller, and carefully retract through the Catheter.
If resistance is felt while retracting forceps, confirm the Catheter is in passive mode. If resistance is still felt consider the following:
a. Ensure the forceps are fully closed.
b. Gently rotate the forceps back and forth while retracting until the resistance is overcome. If resistance persists, or the tool is jammed, remove the Catheter and biopsy tool together.
Syringe
WARNING: Always wear personal protective equipment when removing the Vision Probe, biopsy needle, or bronchoscopic tools from the Catheter tool channel after saline injection. Failure to do so may result in infection if saline regurgitation occurs while removing these items.
CAUTION: Exercise caution if injecting air through the Catheter when the Catheter is in the peripheral airways. Injecting air when the Catheter is wedged in small airways may result in patient harm.
CAUTION: Suction excess fluid injected during broncheoalveolar lavage (BAL), as excess fluid may impair lung function.
1. Use a 20 mL locking syringe to infuse warmed saline (room temperature) through the Catheter tool channel into the airways.
2. Apply suction with the syringe to withdraw the administered saline rinse into the syringe.
Third-Party Bronchoalveolar Lavage Kit
Note: When possible before performing lavage, it is recommended to retract the Catheter so it is away from the airway walls for free fluid flow.
1. Connect the tubing of the bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) container to the narrowed, ribbed portion of the Suction Adapter.
2. Connect the wall suction tubing to the BAL container.
3. Infuse saline with a 20 mL syringe through the Catheter tool channel into the airways.
4. Connect the Suction Adapter, with the BAL container attached, onto the Catheter tool channel.
CAUTION: Do not apply suction for extended durations, as this may impair ventilation or lead to procedure delay.
5. To collect sample into BAL container, apply gentle suction by closing the hole on the suction adapter. Modulate suction strength by partially closing the hole on the suction adapter, or by varying pressure.
6. Disconnect the BAL container from the Catheter and remove from wall suction once sample has been retrieved.
Fiducial Marker Placement Using Third-Party Brush Tool
1. Navigate to the target.
2. Load a compatible fiducial marker onto a compatible brush. The marker should be small enough to fit into the brush sheath, and large enough to fit snug between the sheath and the brush tip.
3. Plug the sheath tip with legally marketed bone wax. This will secure the fiducial marker for deployment.
4. Insert the brush through the Catheter.
5. Using fluoroscopic visualization, push out the fiducial marker from the sheath using the brush tip, and confirm deployment.
6. Remove the brush from the Catheter.
Bronchial Balloons (Endobronchial Blockers)
At the physician's discretion, a blocking balloon may be entered through the Catheter.
1. Insert blocking balloon to desired location.
2. Using fluoroscopic visualization, fill balloon with a mix of saline and legally marketed contrast so it is visible on the fluoroscope.
3. Leave balloon in place as needed.
9.6 Repeat Navigation and Biopsy
1. Navigate to a second target (if applicable).
2. Repeat Navigation and Biopsy steps of the procedure.

10.1 Take Down System
1. Tap the Finish button in the Controller touchscreen to begin on-screen guidance to undock from the patient, remove accessories, clean, and stow the system.
2. Undock from the patient.
a. Retract the Catheter into the ET tube.
b. Retract the Catheter Guide and remove the Catheter from the ET tube.
c. Use the arm clutch button with one hand, and gently pull the Swivel Connector with the other hand to undock the arm and move it out of the way.
3. Remove instruments and accessories.
The number of instrument and accessory uses that remain can be viewed on the bottom monitor.
a. Remove the Vision Probe from the Catheter and uninstall the Vision Probe connector from the arm by rotating and pulling the collar.
b. Remove the Vision Probe Bag by sliding the strap up and over the arm after the Vision Probe has been disconnected.
c. Remove the Catheter from the arm using the Catheter release buttons on the arm.
d. Install the Catheter Reprocessing Cover onto the Catheter (refer to the Ion Instruments Reprocessing Instructions).
e. Remove the Catheter Guide from the arm using the release buttons on the Catheter Guide.
Instrument and Accessory Uses
When instruments and accessories expire, they can no longer be used. Expired instruments, accessories, and any of their components must be properly disposed of following all applicable national and local laws and guidelines.
To view the number of instrument and accessory uses that remain, tap Menu > Accessory Uses on the Controller touchscreen, or view the Accessory Uses panel on the bottom monitor.
10.2 Clean and Disinfect System
Before stowing, follow on-screen guidance to wipe down the System Cart arm and Controller, for visual cleanliness. Clean the rest of the system in accordance with hospital or facility policies.
WARNING: Clean and disinfect both the Controller and System Cart arm after each procedure to prevent cross-contamination that may result in infection.
CAUTION: Do not use these disinfectants on the System Cart or Controller:
· CaviWipes1 (manufactured by Metrex)
· Sani-Cloth AF3 (manufactured by PDI)
Continued use in the presence of cracks may lead to system damage including fluid intrusion and system errors. Contact Customer Service if any cracking is observed.
CAUTION: Do not spray liquids while disinfecting the Ion system. Use only pre-moistened wipes to clean the system. Cleaning with spraying liquids may result in system damage.
Note: Do not manually force the carriage to move unless necessary. Use carriage clutch button or scroll wheel to safely move the carriage.
1. Clean and disinfect the Controller.
WARNING: Properly disinfect the Controller to prevent infection.
a. Remove the trackball and the scroll wheel from Controller.
· If needed, use the magnet attached to the Controller to assist in removing the trackball.
b. Using quaternary ammonium based cleaner disinfectant disposable wipes, follow the wipe manufacturer's instructions to clean and disinfect the trackball, scroll wheel, magnet, and Controller. Roll the scroll wheel to ensure coverage. Ensure the trackball and scroll wheel cups are wiped.
c. After drying, re-insert the trackball and scroll wheel into the Controller.
Note: Calibration initiates after installing the trackball and scroll wheel. Do not touch the trackball or scroll wheel during calibration.
2. Clean and disinfect the arm.
WARNING: Properly disinfect the arm to prevent infection.
a. Ensure all accessories have been removed, and extend the arm fully using the carriage clutch button.
b. Place reusable accessories aside for cleaning. See the Reprocessing Instructions User Manual for further information.
c. Dispose single-use accessories following all applicable national and local laws and guidelines.
d. Using quaternary ammonium based cleaner disinfectant disposable wipes, follow the wipe manufacturer's instructions to clean and disinfect the arm.
Press all raised buttons (that is, Catheter release, powered elevation, and arm clutch buttons) at least five times while wiping the arm (Figure 10.3).
10.3 Stow and Shut Down System
To help prevent collision while transporting the system, properly stow the system cart arm and monitors before shutting the system down. Once the system is shut down, the arm clutch button is inactivated. In an emergency, you can still adjust the arm manually.
CAUTION: Stow the System Cart as instructed. An unbalanced cart may tip over and cause user or patient injury.
To stow the system:
1. Press and hold the arm clutch button to move the arm away from the monitors and create clearance for arm movement.
2. On the Controller touchscreen, tap Start Auto Stow .
This button appears when you swipe the Controller touchscreen to confirm that you cleaned and disinfected the system. If you clean and disinfect the system but then manually collapse the arm before confirming on the touchscreen, the system skips the Auto Stow process. Proceed to Step 3 on page 91.
The arm automatically positions itself vertically and compresses the carriage. If the system errors during this process, contact Customer Service and see Auto Stow Troubleshooting on page 92 for instructions on how to collapse the arm manually.
To stop the arm's movement at any point, tap Stop Auto Stow on the Controller touchscreen. You can choose to continue or cancel the auto stow process.
Once Auto Stow is complete, the monitors display the Stow System guidance.
3. Stow the arm over the base of the cart.
Press and hold the arm clutch button to compact the arm and setup joint as much as possible over the cart base.
4. Stow the monitors over the base of the cart.
Fold the top monitor over the bottom monitor and compact the monitor arm as much as possible over the cart base.
5. Shut down the system by pressing and holding the System Cart Power button for at least three seconds or until the button blinks yellow (the Power button blinks yellow during shutdown).
If the Power button is unresponsive, press and hold the Power button until the system shuts down. If the issue persists, contact Customer Service.
Auto Stow Troubleshooting
If you cannot compress the arm with the Auto Stow button, you can compress the arm manually, even when the system prompts you to proceed with the automated workflow.
To compress the arm manually,
1. Press and hold the powered elevation button to bring the arm to a vertical position.
2. Press and hold the carriage clutch button to compress the arm to its minimal length.
3. Press and hold the arm clutch button to compact the arm and setup joint as much as possible over the cart base.
4. Proceed to Step 4 on page 91 to continue stowing the system.
10.4 Store System
1. Transport the System Cart and Controller to storage.
2. Plug in the System Cart during storage.
Note: Do not store the system in a temperature below -20 ºC or higher than 60 ºC. Exposure to temperature outside the range -20 ºC to 60 °C may damage the product.
Ensure the storage room for the System Cart and the Controller meets the following specifications:
a. Room temperature between 50 to 86 °F (10 to 30 °C).
b. Relative humidity between 10 to 85% non-condensing.

A.2 Mid-procedure Restart
When you restart the system during a procedure, the system preserves your patient plan, registration, target and path selection, and any biopsy markers. The system does not preserve updates to the target and will log out of your Intuitive account if you were previously logged in.
To restart the system during a procedure:
1. If a biopsy tool (for example, needle, forceps, or brush) is advanced through the Catheter tool channel, retract the biopsy tool into its protective sheath and remove it from the Catheter.
2. Keep the Catheter attached to the arm (the Catheter shaft may remain inside the patient). If the Catheter is removed from the arm, you will need to complete Guided Setup and re-register after the system restarts.
3. Keep the system docked to the patient. If the system is undocked, you will need to complete Guided Setup and re-register after the system restarts.
4. If available, tap Restart System on the Controller touchscreen followed by Restart System . Alternatively, you can restart the system manually with the System Cart Power button (press and hold the Power button for three seconds to power off the system; when the system is powered off, press the button again to power the system back on).
Note: Do not unlock the System Cart brakes or move the arm (setup joint) while the system restarts, or else you will be prompted to re-register after completing Guided Setup.
5. When the system powers back on, tap Start Catheter Check if available on the Controller touchscreen.
· If the Start Catheter Check button is not available, skip Step 6 and follow the instructions on the monitors to complete Guided Setup and re-register.
· If the Catheter check fails, skip Step 6 and follow the instructions on the monitors to reattach the Catheter, complete Guided Setup, and re-register.
6. After the Catheter check completes, compare Live View and Navigation View to assess registration.
· To accept registration, tap Continue on the Controller touchscreen.
· To re-do registration, tap Redo Registration on the Controller touchscreen.
A.3 Unexpected System Motion
Note: If the biopsy needle or a biopsy tool is advanced into the tissue through the Catheter tool channel, then pull the needle back into its protecting sheath and into the Catheter before pressing E-stop.
If the system behaves in an unexpected manner that could harm the patient:
1. Press the Emergency stop (E-stop) button on the Controller.
Pressing the E-stop button locks all arm buttons, joints, and brakes. Use force against the arm to move it out of the way if necessary.
2. Once E-stop is pressed, the Catheter will slowly transition into Passive mode. At this time the user can uninstall the Catheter from the arm and manually pull back the Catheter gently from the patient. Proceed with undocking the Swivel Connector from the System Cart.
A.4 Mid-Procedure System Cart or Bed Height Adjustment
WARNING: Do not move patient bed after docking the system to the patient. Moving the patient bed may result in loss of ventilation pathway.
If the System Cart or bed height needs adjustment mid-procedure, undock the system before any adjustment.
1. If a biopsy tool (for example, needle, forceps, or brush) is advanced into tissue through the Catheter tool channel, retract the biopsy tool into its protective sheath and then into the Catheter.
2. Retract the Catheter using scroll wheel or carriage clutch button.
3. Retract the Catheter Guide and remove the Catheter from the ET tube.
4. Use the arm clutch button with one hand, and gently pull the Swivel Connector with the other hand to undock the arm and move it out of the way.
5. Adjust System Cart or bed height as needed.
6. Once adjustments are made, re-dock the system, insert the lubricated Catheter back into the ET tube, extend the Catheter Guide, and advance the Catheter.
7. Perform registration again.
A.5 Unable to Complete Registration
If the survey for one or both of the main bronchi cannot be completed, tap Proceed with Partial Survey on the Controller touchscreen to accept the partial survey and continue to the next step of registration.
If the survey for one or more of the regions cannot be completed, use the Show Lung Regions feature to assist in identifying airways in that region. Then, tap Proceed with Partial Registration on the Controller touchscreen to accept the partial registration and continue to the final step of registration.
Note: You will need to register 4 cm on each side of the main carina to complete registration.
A.6 Registration with Variant Anatomy
If the patient has had a previous resection, use Show Lung Regions to view the corresponding quadrant assignments on the top monitor. Use these quadrant assignments as a guide during registration. If the main carina point is not situated at the anatomical main carina (for example, due to a pneumonectomy), still navigate to this main carina point and begin registration from there. Again, use Show Lung Regions to assist with registration.
If you are unable to complete the quadrant survey, ensure that apical and basal regions of the lung are registered and proceed with partial registration.
If needed, you can review the plan on the Planning Laptop to perform further troubleshooting. See the troubleshooting information in the PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop Supplement.
A.7 Inaccurate Registration (Navigation and Live View Mismatch)
If the Navigation View does not match the Live View and does not allow you to navigate accurately, redo registration.
On the Controller touchscreen, select the Register tab and tap Redo Registration . Confirm your choice on the touchscreen and follow the steps to complete registration again. Consider performing registration under a patient breath hold.
Assess registration accuracy using the Live View, Navigation View, and Tree View.
If the mismatch between the Navigation View and Live View is consistent, especially due to rotational or depth offsets in the periphery of the lungs, use Lock to Path mode to adjust the Navigation View to match the Live View, and then update the target location using Move Target. See and Biopsy Tab on page 41 for more information on the Lock to Path and Move Target functionality.
Error Reading USB
The system cannot read the USB. Try re-inserting the USB. If the issue persists, use a different USB drive.
Note: If a plan has already been loaded when you get this error, you may continue with the loaded plan, but note that you cannot take screenshots, record video, or load new plans unless you restart the system.
USB Not Valid
The system does not recognize the USB. Confirm that a compatible and formatted USB is used. The USB file system should be either FAT/FAT32 or NTFS. If the issue persists after confirming your USB's compatibility and formatting, use a different USB drive.
A.9 Catheter Guide Attachment Errors
If the Catheter Guide is not detected or fails to install, refer to the specific troubleshooting guidance on the system.
If the issue persists after following the system's troubleshooting guidance, you may try the following to recover from the fault:
1. Disconnect and reinstall the Catheter Guide onto the arm. Ensure that the Catheter Guide is fully attached to the arm.
If the issue persists, proceed to Steps 2-4.
2. Disconnect the Catheter Guide from the arm.
3. Clean the Catheter Guide and System arm electrical contacts with an alcohol wipe or dry gauze.
4. Reinstall the Catheter Guide.
If the issue persists, proceed to Steps 5-8.
5. Disconnect the Catheter Guide from the arm.
6. Restart the system.
7. Follow the on-screen prompts to complete the system tests.
8. Reinstall the Catheter Guide.
If the issue persists, proceed to Step 9.
9. Install a new Catheter Guide onto the arm.
A.10 Catheter Tests Fail
If Catheter tests fail, refer to the specific troubleshooting guidance on the system.
To clean the sensor connections on the Catheter and the arm carriage:
1. Check that your Sensor Connection Cleaner has sufficient thread and is functioning properly. Replace the Sensor Connection Cleaner if you observe any of the following:
· Only red spool is visible in the window on the side of the Sensor Connection Cleaner.
· You feel resistance when pushing the handle to the point that the Sensor Connection Cleaner audibly clicks.
· The Sensor Connection Cleaner is not clicking properly.
2. Disconnect the Catheter from the arm.
3. Clean the sensor connections on both the Catheter and the arm carriage using the Sensor Connection Cleaner. Ensure that the Sensor Connection Cleaner is straight when inserted.
4. Reinstall the Catheter.
If the issue persists after following the system's troubleshooting guidance, you may try the following to recover from the fault:
· Repeat cleaning the sensor connections up to two times.
· Reinstall the Catheter Guide:
1. Disconnect the Catheter and Catheter Guide from the arm.
2. Reinstall the Catheter Guide.
3. Clean the sensor connections on both the Catheter and the arm carriage using the Sensor Connection Cleaner.
4. Reinstall the Catheter.
· Restart the system:
1. Disconnect the Catheter from the arm.
2. Restart the system, then follow the on-screen prompts to complete the system tests.
3. Clean the sensor connections on both the Catheter and the arm carriage using the Sensor Connection Cleaner.
4. Reinstall the Catheter.
· Replace the Catheter:
1. Disconnect the Catheter from the arm.
2. Obtain a new Catheter.
3. Clean the sensor connections on both the new Catheter and the arm carriage using the Sensor Connection Cleaner.
4. Install the new Catheter.
A.11 Catheter Not Moving (Controls Unresponsive)
If the Catheter is not moving or the trackball or scroll wheel is not responding, ensure that the Catheter Guide and Swivel Connector are securely connected to the docking spar.
If the Catheter Guide and Swivel Connector are connected to the docking spar, remove the trackball or scroll wheel from its cup, reinstall, and wait for calibration. Clean the trackball or scroll wheel if necessary, and ensure that both are reinstalled fully into their cups.
If the issue persists, try any of the following:
· Clean the Catheter Guide connections.
· Restart the system.
· Install a new Catheter Guide.
A.12 Rotated Vision Probe View (Non-intuitive Driving)
When inserting the Vision Probe through the Catheter, the system will detect the color stripes inside the Catheter to ensure vision is oriented correctly while driving.
If the stripes are not visible, a message appears when the Vision Probe reaches the Catheter tip. The message indicates that orientation was not accurately detected and instructs you to partially retract the Vision Probe until the stripes inside the Catheter are clearly visible, and then reinsert the Vision Probe through the Catheter. Always make sure the Vision Probe tip is clean.
If the system does not present the message because it did not detect the stripes (or if it detects the stripes incorrectly), the Vision Probe image will appear to be 90 or 180 degrees rotated, and driving will be non-intuitive. In this case, partially retract the Vision Probe until the stripes inside the Catheter are clearly visible, and then reinsert the Vision Probe through the Catheter.
If the issue persists, try replacing the Vision Probe, the Catheter, or both.
A.13 Live View Displays Colored Lines
If the Live View (Vision Probe view) on the bottom monitor displays colored lines, install a new Vision Probe onto the system and ensure that the leak test port remains closed. Check the leak test port of the old Vision Probe for fluid or condensation. If no fluid is present, the Vision Probe may have been damaged due to a tight turn or bend radius.
A.14 Vision Probe Image Quality
If the Vision Probe image is not clear, try the following:
WARNING: If saline injection does not clear the obstruction, remove the Catheter or Vision Probe for continued cleaning, as excess saline injection into the lung may result in patient injury.
CAUTION: To prevent impaired lung function, limit the total volume of saline injection for Vision Probe cleaning to less than 40 mL.
CAUTION: Exercise caution if injecting air through the Catheter when the Catheter is in the peripheral airways. Injecting air when the Catheter is wedged in small airways may result in patient harm.
· Inject 0.5 to 2 mL of air or saline into the Catheter tool channel and aspirate back as needed to clear any bubbles.
· Clean the tip of the Vision Probe with isopropyl alcohol.
If the Catheter is retracted into the ET tube, you can remove the Catheter from the ET tube and wipe the tip of the Catheter and Vision Probe together. Otherwise, remove the Vision Probe from the Catheter, wipe the Vision Probe tip, and re-insert the Vision Probe.
· If there are secretions within the Catheter tool channel,
1. Retract the Catheter Guide and remove the Catheter from the ET tube.
2. Remove the Vision Probe from the Catheter.
3. Place the Catheter tip into a bowl of saline.
4. Place the Suction Adapter onto the Catheter tool channel and apply suction.
5. Dry the Catheter by suctioning air through the tool channel.
6. Ensure the Vision Probe is clean and re-insert it into the Catheter.
A.15 Vision Probe Not Detected
If the system does not detect the Vision Probe, remove the Vision Probe and reinstall it. If the issue persists, remove the Vision Probe and install a new Vision Probe. If the Vision Probe is still not detected, restart the system.
A.16 Live View Not Advancing
If the Live View is not advancing or the Swivel Connector disconnects repeatedly, try the following to resolve the issue:
· Adjust the elevation angle of the arm to allow for Swivel Connector connection.
· Re-lubricate the Catheter to reduce tension.
· Monitor drive force during navigation. Elevated drive force may indicate that the Swivel Connector is susceptible to disconnecting from the arm.
A.17 Swivel Connector Disconnects
If the Swivel Connector disconnects repeatedly or the Live View is not advancing, try the following to resolve the issue:
· Adjust the elevation angle of the arm to allow for Swivel Connector connection.
· Re-lubricate the Catheter to reduce tension.
· Monitor drive force during navigation. Elevated drive force may indicate that the Swivel Connector is susceptible to disconnecting from the arm.
A.18 Spinning Wheel on Monitor (Catheter Shape Sensor Interference)
If the top monitor displays a grey spinning wheel during navigation, there is an interruption in the Catheter sensor connection due to a tight bend radius (tight turn in the Catheter tip).
To resolve the issue:
1. If needed, mark the original Catheter position with a biopsy marker.
2. Straighten the Catheter using any of the following methods:
· Articulate the trackball in the direction of the white arrow that is displayed on the tip indicator.
· Press the Passive button on the Controller.
· Slightly retract the Catheter.
If the issue persists, the following may improve tight turn navigation:
· Re-lubricate the Catheter.
· Undock and retract the ET tube (which requires re-registering). This gives the Catheter more length beyond the tip of the ET tube, which allows the Catheter to build more support against the trachea wall to make a wider turn.
Under fluoroscopy, monitor the Catheter and look for a delay in Catheter advancement as indication that you are building support against the trachea wall.
· Use the carriage clutch button to retract the carriage and release tension.
A.19 Touchscreen Unresponsive
If the Controller touchscreen is unresponsive, the system may detect fluid on the screen. Wipe any visible fluid from the screen and wait five seconds before attempting to make a selection. Otherwise, wait five seconds before making a selection.
If the issue persists, restart the system.
A.20 System Monitors Black Out (Time Out)
When the System Cart monitors stop displaying feed (time out), the Catheter maintains its position. To recover the monitor feed, troubleshoot as follows:
Note: After performing the troubleshooting steps below, if only one monitor returns to a live feed, perform a mid-procedure restart to resolve the issue. See A.2 Mid-procedure Restart on page 94.
· If the monitors time out during the procedure and the monitor timeout notification appears, select Recover on the Controller touchscreen to resolve the issue.
· If the monitors time out when you plug in or unplug an external display or recording device from the System Cart, select Continue on the Controller touchscreen to synchronize the monitors, and then select Recover to resolve the issue.
A.21 System Faults
When a system fault occurs, the system displays a message on the monitor, the instrument arm locks, and the Catheter becomes inactive.
WARNING: When a system fault occurs, retract the tool inside the protective sheath immediately to minimize interaction with tissue and prevent patient injury as the Catheter slowly relaxes in response to the fault.
CAUTION: Failure to recognize and recover from system faults may result in procedure delay.
Non-Recoverable Fault
In the event of a non-recoverable fault, system LEDs illuminate red (if applicable). See A.2 Midprocedure Restart on page 94. If the fault persists, contact Customer Service to troubleshoot the issue.
Recoverable Fault
In the event of a recoverable fault, system LEDs illuminate yellow on the part of the system that needs attention to recover the fault (if applicable). Follow system messages to recover and continue with the procedure. Or, tap Recover Fault on the Controller touchscreen.
A.22 Patient Motion
The system detects if there is significant patient motion, and shows a notification on the top monitor. If patient motion is detected, evaluate registration accuracy by ensuring the Live View matches with the Navigation View while driving. Perform one of the following steps:
· If registration is accurate, tap Dismiss .
· If registration is not accurate, tap Redo Registration to perform registration again.
Note: Catheter buckling or excessive friction in the ET tube may be detected as patient motion, and result in a patient motion notification from the system. Ensure sufficient lubrication is applied to the Catheter.
A.23 Mid-Procedure Catheter Exchange
1. If a biopsy tool (for example, needle, forceps, or brush) is advanced through the Catheter tool channel, retract the biopsy tool into its protective sheath and then remove it from the Catheter.
2. Retract the Catheter into the ET tube using the scroll wheel or carriage clutch button.
3. Retract the Catheter Guide.
4. Pull the Catheter out of the ET tube to remove the Catheter from the patient.
5. Remove Vision Probe from the Catheter, but keep it connected to the arm.
6. Disconnect the Catheter from the arm.
7. Tap Continue Procedure on the Controller touchscreen.
8. Raise the arm carriage, if needed.
9. Get a new Catheter, and then clean the sensor connections on the new Catheter and on the arm carriage using the Sensor Connection Cleaner (see Step 2 on page 60 and Step 3 on page 61).
10. Install the new Catheter and allow the Catheter self-tests to complete.
11. Insert the Vision Probe into the Catheter tool channel.
12. Lubricate the Catheter, and insert the Catheter into the ET tube.
13. Extend the Catheter Guide, and advance the Catheter.
14. Perform registration.
Check Connections
In case of inconsistent power behavior, first check AC power connections:
1. Confirm the power cable is properly connected to a dedicated AC power outlet.
2. Confirm the power breaker switch is On (indicated by an 'I' near the switch). The power breaker switch is on the back of the System Cart.
Battery Backup
Before starting a procedure, the system must be plugged in to mains power.
If the System Cart is unplugged from mains power during a procedure, the system alerts you that it is running on battery power and advises you to plug the System Cart into mains power to avoid loss of power.
If the system loses mains power during a procedure:
1. System use can continue but is not recommended. Once the battery reaches its lowest point, the system will shut down.
Note: Battery backup is only intended for safe removal of the system components from the patient and is not intended for continuing a procedure.

1.1 How to Use this Manual
This user manual provides information specific to the use of the Ion endoluminal system, instruments, and accessories.

This user manual presents representative images of the system, instruments, accessories, and user interface. The representative images provide instruction on the use of the product. In some cases, the aesthetics or dimensions of the device shown in the representative images may be different from the product in use.

Note: Follow all instructions for use (IFUs) supplied with the system, its components, instruments and accessories, including the PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop Supplement, the Reprocessing Instructions, and any IFUs provided with third-party instruments or accessories. IFUs are also referred to as user manuals.
Note: Not all technologies may have regulatory approval or may be commercially available in all geographies. For availability in your country, check with your local representative.
1.2 Limitation on Use - Limited License

Ion endoluminal system instruments and accessories are provided pursuant to a limited license to use only with the Ion endoluminal system. Upon expiration of the instrument's or accessory's maximum number of uses, this limited license expires. Any repair, refurbishment, reconditioning, or servicing of Intuitive instruments and accessories is strictly prohibited and results in expiration of limited license.
Contact Information
Use the following information for customer service, including ordering, reporting complaints or adverse events, and general information regarding Intuitive products and services.

Use the following information if the system requires maintenance or service. Preventive maintenance is required and must be performed by authorized Intuitive personnel. There are no user-serviceable parts on the main system components.
In the U.S., phones are staffed Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. Eastern Time (ET) to 6 p.m. Pacific Time (PT).
In Europe, phones are staffed Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. Central European Time (CET).
About this Manual
This manual uses the following conventions.
· Names of labeled items that appear on hardware or on screen are in bold ( Volume ).
· A greater than > sign indicates the path of progression through menu options ( Settings > Video Output ).
· Blue text is used for cross-references. In electronic versions, cross-references are active, clickable links.
Essential Prescribing Information
· Device Name: Intuitive Ion Endoluminal System and Instruments (IF1000).
· Rx only: Federal Law (USA) restricts this device to sale by or on the order of a physician (or properly licensed practitioner).
Indications for Use

The Ion endoluminal system (Model IF1000), referred to in this manual as 'the system,' assists the user in navigating a catheter and endoscopic tools in the pulmonary tract using endoscopic visualization of the tracheobronchial tree for diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. The Ion endoluminal system enables fiducial marker placement. It does not make a diagnosis and is not for pediatric use.
The PlanPoint Software uses patient CT scans to create a 3D plan of the lung and navigation pathways for use with the Ion endoluminal system.
The Flexision Biopsy Needle is used with the Ion endoluminal system to biopsy tissue from a target area in the lung.
Intended Use
The Ion System Cart (referred to as the System Cart) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract.
The Ion Controller (referred to as the Controller) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract.

The Ion Fully Articulating Catheter (referred to as the Catheter) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system for navigating to the target region in the airways. It is intended to also provide a conduit for the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe, Flexision Biopsy Needles and delivering compatible off-the-shelf tools.
The Flexision Biopsy Needle is intended to retrieve tissue from a target structure.
The Ion Peripheral Vision Probe (referred to as the Vision Probe) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system to provide live airway view for catheter navigation.
The Vision Probe Adapter is intended to be used to connect the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter.
The Vision Probe Bag is used for temporary storage of the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe during a procedure.
The Catheter Guide is intended to be used with the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to provide support.
The Sensor Connection Cleaner is used for cleaning the sensor connections on the carriage of the Ion System Cart and the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter.
The Swivel Connector is intended to be used to connect the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to an endotracheal tube.
The Suction Adapter is intended to allow modulation of suction when suction tubing is connected to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter.
Intended Patient Population
The Ion endoluminal system (Model IF1000) is intended for adult patients suitable for bronchoscopy.

Patient general health and medical history must be adequately assessed along with potential benefits and risks prior to performing procedures with the Ion endoluminal system. These include but are not limited to risks associated with pulmonary disease, severe pulmonary hypertension, cardiovascular disease, bleeding disorders, thromboembolic disorders, anticoagulation therapy, anatomical constraints, inability to oxygenate and patient suitability for general anesthesia.
Intended User
Only physicians with adequate training and experience in bronchoscopic techniques and adequate healthcare facilities should perform procedures with the Ion endoluminal system.

Training provided by Intuitive is limited to the use of the Ion endoluminal system and does not replace the necessary medical training and experience required to perform diagnostic and therapeutic bronchoscopy procedures.
Clinical Risks and Benefits

Patients should talk to their physician to decide if the Ion endoluminal system is right for them. As with any bronchoscopic procedure under general anesthesia, serious complications may include bleeding, pneumothorax (collapsed lung), cardiac-related complications, respiratory failure, air embolism, or death. As with other medical procedures, there may be additional risks associated with the use of general anesthesia and/or endotracheal intubation which are not listed above; patients should consult a healthcare professional regarding these and other potential risks.

The overall benefit of the Ion endoluminal system is to bronchoscopically access and biopsy pulmonary lesions, including nodules in the lung periphery. The potential clinical benefits include improved or similar diagnostic outcomes of the sample obtained with comparable or fewer complications to other non-surgical approaches. The clinical benefits depend on a number of factors, including but not limited to nodule characteristics, patient medical history and disease state, and physician experience.
1.5 Serious Incident Reporting
Serious incident means any incident that directly or indirectly led, might have led, or might lead to any of the following:
· the death of a patient, user, or other person,
· the temporary or permanent serious deterioration of a patient's, user's, or other person's state of health,
· a serious public health threat.

For a patient/user/third party in the European Union and in countries with identical regulatory regime (Regulation 2017/745/EU on Medical Devices); if, during the use of this device or as a result of its use, a serious incident has occurred, report the incident to the manufacturer and its authorized representative and to your national authority.

Warnings
WARNING: Before using the Ion endoluminal system (the system), review and understand the content in this manual and all accompanying manuals and supplements.
WARNING: To prevent patient harm, use only instruments, accessories, and third-party products that are approved by Intuitive. Non-approved devices are not guaranteed to be compatible with the system.

WARNING: Confirm that the sterile packaging for all single-use devices is intact and sealed before use. Do not use contaminated single-use devices or reuse single-use devices, as this may result in patient infection or equipment damage.
WARNING: To avoid risk of electric shock or equipment damage, do not step on, crush/ pinch, crimp, or otherwise stress cables and connectors.

WARNING: Do not reuse or reprocess single-use devices (such as the Swivel Connector and Vision Probe Adapter) after being removed from package, even if unused, as this may result in patient infection or device damage.

WARNING: To prevent impaired ventilation and patient injury, the procedure should be performed under general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation, Electrocardiography (ECG) monitoring, and ventilator alarms.

WARNING: If the system, instruments and accessories, or any of their components cannot be manipulated in a precise and controlled manner, discontinue use and contact Intuitive to prevent patient harm.
WARNING: To prevent patient injury, do not use excessive force during the insertion or extraction of the Vision Probe or bronchoscopic tools through the Catheter tool channel.
WARNING: Use fluoroscopic visualization (fluoroscopy) when advancing tools past the tip of the Catheter. Failure to use fluoroscopy during biopsy may result in patient injury.
WARNING: Advance the Catheter only under live visualization from the Vision Probe (Live View) to prevent procedural delay or patient injury.
WARNING: Do not activate the scroll wheel while interacting with the Controller touchscreen, as this may result in pneumothorax.
WARNING: In the event of a medical emergency, follow steps to obtain immediate access to the patient (emergency egress), to avoid delays in patient care.
WARNING: Do not contaminate instruments or accessories before or during use, as contamination may result in patient infection.
WARNING:
Handle biopsy needles with care to prevent user injury.
WARNING: Always inspect the biopsy needle for damage before and during use. A damaged needle can contain loose fragments that may cause toxic reaction if left in the patient.
WARNING: Use caution during biopsy of targets within 5 mm of the visceral pleura or other critical structures. Biopsy near critical structures may result in patient injury.
WARNING: Insert the Vision Probe after biopsy to assess airways for trauma or bleeding to prevent delayed intervention in case of an emergency.
WARNING: Follow proper system and Controller cleaning procedures to prevent patient infection.
Cautions

CAUTION: The system may be unpacked, installed, and serviced by Intuitive personnel only. Do not attempt to unpack, install, or service equipment without Intuitive personnel, as this may result in user harm.
CAUTION: No modification of this equipment is allowed. Failure to comply may result in user or patient harm.
CAUTION: To avoid the risk of electric shock, this equipment must only be connected to a supply mains with protective earth.
CAUTION: Note that conversion to alternate technique during the procedure may prolong anesthesia time.

CAUTION: Leakage current from interconnected medical equipment (for example, ultrasound equipment) may exceed safe levels. To maintain the safety of patients and users, interconnect only with devices that comply with IEC 60601-1, and whose total patient leakage current meets the limits of Clause 16 of IEC 60601-1 (third edition or higher).

CAUTION: Leakage current from interconnected electrical equipment (for example, external displays) may exceed safe levels. To maintain the safety of patients and users, interconnect only with devices in compliance with IEC 60601-1-1. Users must ensure that any interconnected equipment not supplied by Intuitive maintains compliance with IEC 60601-1-1.
CAUTION: Do not cover any ventilation openings on the system or on the arm. Covering ventilation openings may cause improper function of the system.
CAUTION: Inspect all instruments and accessories for potential damage prior to clinical use to prevent procedure delay.
CAUTION: Exercise caution when inserting the biopsy needle into the Catheter tool channel with the sheath extended. Failure to do so may result in patient injury.
CAUTION: To prevent impaired lung function, limit the total volume of saline injection for Vision Probe cleaning to less than 40 mL.

CAUTION: If resistance is felt when removing the Vision Probe or tool from the Catheter tool channel, do not continue retracting the device, as this may result in device damage. Remove the Catheter and Vision Probe or tool together.
Notes

Note: The Ion system, instruments, and accessories are not intended specifically to control, diagnose, monitor, or correct a defect of the heart, central circulatory, or central nervous system through direct contact with those parts of the body.
Note: Always route the system cables away from possible tripping and stepping situations.

Note: Before connecting any fluoroscopy equipment having no patient applied parts (that is, nothing comes into direct contact with patient) with this system, use device labeling to confirm that they comply with the standards IEC 60601-1 and IEC 60601-1-3.
Note: All reusable devices must be reprocessed before use.
Note: Use only water-based or silicone-based lubricants for the Catheter. Other lubricants may be difficult to remove during reprocessing and reduce the effectiveness of disinfection.
Note: Navigation View should be used as guidance only.
Note: Drive with caution in small airways where the airway diameter is smaller than the outer diameter of the Catheter.
Note: Do not apply large volume suction through the Catheter tool channel when Catheter tip is wedged in small airways.
Endoscopic Procedure Precautions and Notes

Only physicians having adequate training and experience with endoscopic techniques should perform endoscopic procedures with the Ion endoluminal system. Medical literature should be consulted regarding techniques, complications, and hazards before performing any endoscopic procedure.

CAUTION: High energy radiated light may be transmitted from the Vision Probe tip. High temperatures may exist in front of the light emission window. Exercise caution when positioning the tip of the Vision Probe to minimize tissue exposure to heat emitted from the light.
Note: Use of the Ion endoluminal system may be associated with increased procedure and anesthesia time.
Accessory Equipment Interconnection

WARNING: Leakage currents from other medical equipment applied parts may be additive. To ensure maximum safety for the patient, only devices having Type BF or Type CF applied parts should be used with the Ion endoluminal system.
Laser Safety
Class 1 Laser Product: The IF1000 System Cart is equipped with a subassembly, which was determined to be a CLASS 1 LASER PRODUCT, which has been tested to the IEC 60825-1 Ed. 2 (2007) standard.

CAUTION: While Class 1 laser products are considered to be 'eye safe' without the need for additional protection, the following general safety guidelines should be observed to reduce the risk of eye injury:
· Do not look or stare at optical fiber ports or optical fibers that are connected to a light source.

· Do not examine with optical instruments optical fiber ports or optical fibers that are connected to a source. The use of optical instruments (for example, a magnifying glass) may increase eye hazard.

· Do not attempt to perform any repair or maintenance on optical communication components. Repairs and maintenance outside that which is allowed herein must be performed only by an authorized repair facility.

Chapter 2 System Software Updates

When the system is connected to OnSite, the system notifies you when a software update is available. The software version available for installation is listed at the top of the About screen on the Controller (Figure 2.1).

We recommend installing system software updates when they become available. However, it is important to perform software updates when they will not disrupt patient procedures, such as at the end of the day or on a day when no procedures are scheduled. Once started, a software update cannot be canceled, and the system will be inoperable until the update completes. If the software update results in a non-recoverable error, the system will be non-functional until an Intuitive representative can assist.
Once all Ion systems at a site have been updated to the latest system software, any software updates for the Planning Laptop are then made available.
2.1 Updating the System Software

Before you start a software update, we recommend informing all personnel who may handle or encounter the system during the update. During a software update, actions such as powering down the system or disconnecting the system from the Controller or power may cause the system to become non-functional, requiring the assistance of an Intuitive representative before the system can be used again.
To update the system software:
1. Ensure that the system is in the proper state:
· The system is powered on.
· The system is connected to AC power.
· The system is connected to the Controller.
· The System Cart arm is stowed.
· The battery is charged to at least 80%.
· No instruments or accessories are installed on the system.
2. On the Controller, tap Menu > About > Go to Update , or tap Go to Update if available from a system prompt.
3. On the prompt, tap Continue to acknowledge that the system must remain connected to power and to the Controller for the duration of the update.

4. On the next prompt, note the estimated duration of the update and ensure that the system will not be needed during this time. Once started, the update cannot be canceled, and the system will be inoperable until the update completes.
5. Tap Start Update (Figure 2.2) to begin the software update.
Once the update begins, note the guidance to keep the system powered on and connected to the Controller for the duration of the update.
Allow the software update to complete. Do not touch the system during this time.
While the update is in progress, the system LEDs blink yellow. When update completes, the system automatically restarts.
Note: If the system errors at any point during the update or does not restart, contact Customer Service. Do not restart or unplug the system from the Controller or AC power.
7. After the system restarts, note the confirmation prompt that appears:
· If the software update was successful, tap Close on the confirmation prompt to proceed with normal system use.
· If the software update could not be completed, the system rolls back to its previous software version. Tap Close on the confirmation prompt to proceed with normal system use.
End of Section

4.1 Device Description
The Ion endoluminal system navigates a flexible Catheter within the lung to a planned path in order to sample a target. It is comprised of the following components, instruments, and accessories:
(continues on next page)
PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop

PlanPoint Software generates a plan of the patient's airways from an existing CT scan, and the Planning Laptop is a portable computer used with the PlanPoint Software. The CT scan images are uploaded to the PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop and segmented by the software. After identifying the target, the user can add a path to the target. The user can modify or create additional targets and paths as needed. The patient plan is transferred from the Planning Laptop to the Controller and displayed on the System Cart monitors for navigational guidance during the procedure.

Protected Health Information and Personal Data: Patient and surgeon information, including names, birth dates, and imaging study dates, are fictitious. In compliance with the U.S. Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and its foreign counterparts, no actual protected health information or personal data is used in this manual.
For additional information on PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop use, see the PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop Supplement.
Ion System Cart

The Ion System Cart (referred to as the System Cart) consists of the instrument arm (with carriage), setup joint, brakes, and monitors (top and bottom). The instrument arm (referred to as the arm) adjusts to move the Catheter through the airway. The monitors present navigational information such as live video (Live View) from the Vision Probe, Navigation View, and biopsy target information. Third-party video sources including bronchoscope, fluoroscope, and radial endobronchial ultrasound (R-EBUS) can also be displayed on the monitors.
For further information on System Cart use, see 4.2 System Cart Use on page 33.
Ion Controller
The Ion Controller (referred to as the Controller) is used by the physician to control insertion, retraction, and articulation of the Catheter, and to view information displayed on the touchscreen.
For further information on Controller use, see 4.3 Controller Use on page 39.
Ion Fully Articulating Catheter
1. Housing
2. Sensor port
3. Input discs
4. Electrical contacts
5. Shaft
6. Tool channel entrance
7. Tool channel exit (tip)

The Ion Fully Articulating Catheter (referred to as the Catheter) has an approximately 3.5 mm outer diameter (at the tip), and a 2 mm tool channel that allows for insertion of compatible tools. It is compatible with the Vision Probe, Flexision biopsy needles, and third-party tools. The fiber optic shape sensor in the Catheter provides the shape and position of the Catheter on the System Cart monitors. The Catheter has an articulating tip.
The Catheter consists of the housing, sensor, input discs, shaft, tool channel, and tip.
The Catheter is provided non-sterile and is a multi-use device. See the Ion Instruments Reprocessing Instructions for further information.

The Ion Peripheral Vision Probe (referred to as the Vision Probe) is an endoscope that is compatible with, and inserted into, the 2.0 mm Catheter tool channel. The Vision Probe provides direct visualization of the patient's airways during navigation.
The Vision Probe consists of the lens (tip), shaft, Vision Probe Adapter (Figure 4.7, installed separately), cable adapter, leak test port, connector, and cable.

The light emitting diode (LED) for the Vision Probe is located at the connector, and the light fibers carry the light from the LED to the tip to illuminate the airways. The direction of view of the tip is zero degrees. The field of view is 120 degrees. The Vision Probe has no user-serviceable parts.
The Vision Probe is provided non-sterile and is a multi-use device. See the Ion Instruments Reprocessing Instructions for further information.
Vision Probe Adapter

The Vision Probe Adapter attaches the Vision Probe to the Catheter. The saline flush port allows for saline injection for cleaning during the procedure. It is a single-use accessory that is attached to the Vision Probe (Figure 4.6) before use. The Vision Probe Adapter should be removed and disposed of prior to reprocessing.
The Vision Probe Adapter is a single-use device provided sterile by Ethylene Oxide (EO) sterilization method. For replacement, contact Customer Service.
WARNING: If saline injection does not clear the obstruction, remove the Catheter or Vision Probe for continued cleaning, as excess saline injection into the lung may result in patient injury.
Vision Probe Bag

The Vision Probe Bag installs over the arm for temporary storage of the Vision Probe when it is not inserted within the Catheter tool channel. The Vision Probe Bag is a single-use device provided sterile by Ethylene Oxide (EO) sterilization method. For replacement, contact Customer Service.
Suction Adapter
The Suction Adapter attaches to the Catheter tool channel to be used with suction tubing for bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL).
The Suction Adapter is a single-use device provided sterile by Ethylene Oxide (EO) sterilization method. For replacement, contact Customer Service.
CAUTION: Do not apply suction for extended durations, as this may impair ventilation or lead to procedure delay.
Note: Do not suction excess fluid in airways when vision is obscured. While the Catheter tip is wedged in small airways, bubbles may form that can obscure vision and lead to procedure delay.
Catheter Guide
The Catheter Guide prevents buckling of the Catheter shaft during insertion into the patient. The Catheter Guide attaches to the arm and has release buttons to remove it from the arm.
The Catheter Guide consists of the proximal mount, release buttons, eyelets, links, hinges, Catheter channel entrance and exit points, and a distal mount.
The Catheter Guide is provided non-sterile and is a multi-use device. See the Ion Catheter Guide Reprocessing Instructions for further information.
Swivel Connector

The Swivel Connector magnetically connects the endotracheal tube (ET tube) and the ventilator assembly to the arm. This allows the Catheter to pass into the airway. This provides a secure anchor to the patient. The Swivel Connector is docked to the distal mount of the arm. To maintain ventilation when no Catheter or bronchoscope is present, the connector has a self-sealing valve or, the attached plug may be inserted. The Swivel Connector is compatible with bronchoscopes from the diameter of the Fully Articulating Catheter up to a 7.0 mm standard bronchoscope.
The Swivel Connector is a single-use device provided sterile by Ethylene Oxide (EO) sterilization method. For replacement, contact Customer Service.
Flexision Biopsy Needles
1. Needle stroke length markings

The Flexision Biopsy Needles (referred to as biopsy needles, or needles) are flexible needles compatible with the Catheter. Biopsy needles come in 19G, 21G, and 23G sizes and are protected by a flexible retractable sheath, with a stylet for support during insertion. The needle and sheath tip are radiopaque for visualization under fluoroscopy. The needle handle contains a catch (detent) that creates resistance to hold the handle in place until the user pushes the handle past the catch (detent). The needle stop allows the user to control the needle length (up to 3 cm). The biopsy needles are packaged with a compatible three-way valve and vacuum syringe.
The biopsy needles are single-use devices provided sterile by Ethylene Oxide (EO) sterilization method. For replacement, contact Customer Service.

Instrument Arm Features
1. Elevation clutch button (non-powered) : Press and hold to adjust the arm elevation (up or down). Non-powered elevation helps the user reach the tool channel for instrument exchanges and biopsies.
2. Biopsy marker button : Press the button to place a simulated marker at the tip of the Catheter in the Navigation View. The biopsy marker is used to identify a precise sample location.
3. Catheter release buttons : Press to release (uninstall) the Catheter from the arm.

4. Powered elevation button : Press the up arrow or the down arrow to adjust the arm elevation (up or down). Powered elevation helps the user reach the arm for instrument installation, docking, cleaning, etcetera.

5. Arm clutch button : Press and hold to move the arm to the desired location. This positions the setup joint of the arm, which is the part of the arm that determines the docking position to the patient.
6. Carriage clutch button : Press and hold to lower or raise the carriage. Using the carriage clutch puts the Catheter into passive mode.

System Cart Monitors

This section provides an overview of the System Cart monitor interface for guidance during the procedure. The following configurations are possible: Camera (Vision Probe view), Camera & Fluoro (Vision Probe view and live fluoroscope), R-EBUS & Fluoro, and Bronchoscope.
1. Anatomy Border : Displays marked anatomical structures to be referenced during the procedure.
2. Tree View : Displays a 3D reconstruction of the airway tree from the patient CT scan, or the Catheter's current shape.
3. Workflow step : Displays procedure workflow step (for example, Guided Setup).
4. Patient information : Displays patient information.
5. Orientation guide : Top monitor: Indicates the orientation of the Tree View.
6. Optimal fluoroscopy angle : Displays suggested angle for the fluoroscope, for optimal view of Catheter tip and needle advancement during biopsy.
7. Drive force : Displays an estimation of force measured at the back end of the Catheter.
8. Progress View : Displays Catheter progress towards target, and tight bends along the Catheter shaft.
9. Banner notification area : Displays notifications.
10. Orientation guide : Bottom monitor: Indicates the direction (anterior, posterior, medial, lateral, superior, inferior) the Catheter tip is pointing in the patient.
11. Distance to target (near and far edge) : Displays the distance to the near edge and far edge of the target from the Catheter tip.
12. Distance to anatomy border : Displays the distance to the anatomical boundary identified during planning. For more information, see the PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop Supplement.
13. Distance to reference area : Displays the distance to the near edge, far edge, and point of the closest visible reference area, which is highlighted in Navigation View.
14. Bend radius : Displays the Catheter bend radius.
15. Tip indicator : Displays Catheter tip bend direction.
16. Live View : Displays live video from the Vision Probe.
17. Navigation View : Displays simulated endobronchial view from the CT scan. Preview: Displays a preview to a planned path in the Navigation View.
18. Endoluminal Compass : Directional indicators (anterior, posterior, medial, lateral, superior, inferior) that display over the Navigation View and around the orientation guide.
4.3 Controller Use
The Controller provides controls to insert, retract, and articulate the Catheter.
Note: If friction is felt in the trackball or scroll wheel, clean it with saline and dry with gauze prior to or during use, as needed.
Note: Calibration initiates after installing the trackball and scroll wheel. Do not touch the trackball or scroll wheel during calibration.
Note: If Controller responsiveness is poor, change or dry gloves. The Controller touchscreen and scroll wheel are designed to sense touch. Wet gloves may interfere with touch sensing.
The Controller has the following components:
1. Handle : Provides grasp for transport of the Controller.
2. Emergency stop (E-stop) button : Stops system operation at any time and causes the Catheter tip to go inactive.
3. Scroll wheel : Controls the insertion and retraction of the Catheter. Roll it towards the touchscreen to insert the Catheter, and roll it away from the touchscreen to retract it.

4. Passive button : Controls the Catheter state (active and passive). Quick-press this button to relax the Catheter tip (passive), and press it again to resume active mode. Press and hold to slowly relax the Catheter tip (temporary passive). Release the button to stop relaxing the Catheter and resume active mode.
5. Touchscreen : Controls to select targets, save images and videos, and provide other options described in this manual.

6. Trackball : Controls the articulation of the Catheter tip. Roll the trackball right to move the Catheter tip to the right, roll the trackball left to move the Catheter tip to the left. Roll up and down to move the Catheter tip up and down.
7. USB inputs : Connects the USB storage device to the Controller. There are two options: USB-A and USB-C. Either input can be used, depending on the connector type.
8. Magnet : A magnet attached to the Controller that can be used to remove the trackball.
9. Height adjustment foot pedal : Adjusts the Controller height up or down.
10. Brakes : Locks the wheels in place. There is one brake on each wheel.
