cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_20
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: The system may be unpacked, installed, and serviced by Intuitive personnel only. Do not attempt to unpack, install, or service equipment without Intuitive personnel, as this may result in user harm.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_21
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: No modification of this equipment is allowed. Failure to comply may result in user or patient harm.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_22
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: To avoid the risk of electric shock, this equipment must only be connected to a supply mains with protective earth.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_23
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Note that conversion to alternate technique during the procedure may prolong anesthesia time.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_24
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Leakage current from interconnected medical equipment (for example, ultrasound equipment) may exceed safe levels. To maintain the safety of patients and users, interconnect only with devices that comply with IEC 60601-1, and whose total patient leakage current meets the limits of Clause 16 of IEC 60601-1 (third edition or higher).

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_25
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Leakage current from interconnected electrical equipment (for example, external displays) may exceed safe levels. To maintain the safety of patients and users, interconnect only with devices in compliance with IEC 60601-1-1. Users must ensure that any interconnected equipment not supplied by Intuitive maintains compliance with IEC 60601-1-1.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_26
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Do not cover any ventilation openings on the system or on the arm. Covering ventilation openings may cause improper function of the system.

cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Inspect all instruments and accessories for potential damage prior to clinical use to prevent procedure delay.

cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Exercise caution when inserting the biopsy needle into the Catheter tool channel with the sheath extended. Failure to do so may result in patient injury.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_29
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: To prevent impaired lung function, limit the total volume of saline injection for Vision Probe cleaning to less than 40 mL.

cautions.text: If resistance is felt when removing the Vision Probe or tool from the Catheter tool channel, do not continue retracting the device, as this may result in device damage. Remove the Catheter and Vision Probe or tool together.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_39
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: High energy radiated light may be transmitted from the Vision Probe tip. High temperatures may exist in front of the light emission window. Exercise caution when positioning the tip of the Vision Probe to minimize tissue exposure to heat emitted from the light.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_42

cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Do not apply suction for extended durations, as this may impair ventilation or lead to procedure delay.

cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Use small size syringes (for example, 12 mL or smaller) to prevent accidentally injecting large volumes of saline or air and impairing lung function.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_67
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Inspect all instruments and accessories for potential damage prior to clinical use to prevent procedure delay.

cautions.text: Inspect the Vision Probe for defects or damage to tip or lens, fiber optic surfaces and cable prior to inserting into the Catheter tool channel. Failure to do so may result in patient harm or Catheter damage.

cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: If fluid is observed in the sensor port well on the Catheter Reprocessing Cover or on the green sensor port, do not install the Catheter on the system, as it may result in Catheter or system damage. Contact Customer Service.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_76
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Use small size syringes (for example, 12 mL or smaller) to prevent accidentally injecting large volumes of saline or air and impairing lung function.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_82
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: If fluid is found on the green sensor port while cleaning with Sensor Connection Cleaner, do not install the Catheter on the system, as it may result in Catheter or system damage. Contact Customer Service.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_98
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: If resistance is felt when removing the Vision Probe or tool from the Catheter tool channel, do not continue retracting the device, as this may result in device damage. Remove the Catheter and Vision Probe or tool together.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_104
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Proceed with caution if the biopsy needle is inserted or removed through a Catheter bend radius smaller than 15 mm. Insertion and removal of the biopsy needle should not be performed against increased resistance. Failure to follow instructions may result in Catheter or needle damage.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_105
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Exercise caution when inserting the biopsy needle into the Catheter tool channel with the sheath extended. Failure to do so may result in patient injury.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_114
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Exercise caution if injecting air through the Catheter when the Catheter is in the peripheral airways. Injecting air when the Catheter is wedged in small airways may result in patient harm.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_115
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Suction excess fluid injected during broncheoalveolar lavage (BAL), as excess fluid may impair lung function.

cautions.text: Do not apply suction for extended durations, as this may impair ventilation or lead to procedure delay.

cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Do not use these disinfectants on the System Cart or Controller:

cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Do not spray liquids while disinfecting the Ion system. Use only pre-moistened wipes to clean the system. Cleaning with spraying liquids may result in system damage.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_125
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Stow the System Cart as instructed. An unbalanced cart may tip over and cause user or patient injury.

cautions.text: To prevent impaired lung function, limit the total volume of saline injection for Vision Probe cleaning to less than 40 mL.

cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Exercise caution if injecting air through the Catheter when the Catheter is in the peripheral airways. Injecting air when the Catheter is wedged in small airways may result in patient harm.

cautions.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_137
cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: Failure to recognize and recover from system faults may result in procedure delay.

cautions.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
cautions.text: The Live View video signal from the Vision Probe may be susceptible to interference from devices that transmit in the frequency of 80-90 MHz. If excessive noise is seen in the Live View, reorient or relocate the system or the interfering equipment to increase the distance between the two pieces of equipment.

notes.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_1
notes.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
notes.text: Follow all instructions for use (IFUs) supplied with the system, its components, instruments and accessories, including the PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop Supplement, the Reprocessing Instructions, and any IFUs provided with third-party instruments or accessories. IFUs are also referred to as user manuals.

notes.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
notes.text: Not all technologies may have regulatory approval or may be commercially available in all geographies. For availability in your country, check with your local representative.

notes.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_31
notes.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
notes.text: The Ion system, instruments, and accessories are not intended specifically to control, diagnose, monitor, or correct a defect of the heart, central circulatory, or central nervous system through direct contact with those parts of the body.

notes.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_32
notes.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
notes.text: Always route the system cables away from possible tripping and stepping situations.

notes.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_33
notes.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
notes.text: Before connecting any fluoroscopy equipment having no patient applied parts (that is, nothing comes into direct contact with patient) with this system, use device labeling to confirm that they comply with the standards IEC 60601-1 and IEC 60601-1-3.

notes.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_34
notes.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
notes.text: All reusable devices must be reprocessed before use.

notes.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
notes.text: Use only water-based or silicone-based lubricants for the Catheter. Other lubricants may be difficult to remove during reprocessing and reduce the effectiveness of disinfection.

notes.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
notes.text: Navigation View should be used as guidance only.

notes.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
notes.text: Drive with caution in small airways where the airway diameter is smaller than the outer diameter of the Catheter.

notes.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_38
notes.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
notes.text: Do not apply large volume suction through the Catheter tool channel when Catheter tip is wedged in small airways.

notes.text: Use of the Ion endoluminal system may be associated with increased procedure and anesthesia time.

notes.text: If the system errors at any point during the update or does not restart, contact Customer Service. Do not restart or unplug the system from the Controller or AC power.

notes.text: Follow all instructions for use (IFUs) supplied with the system, its components, instruments and accessories, including the PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop Supplement, the reprocessing instructions, and any IFUs provided with third-party instruments or accessories. notes.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_48
notes.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
notes.text: Do not suction excess fluid in airways when vision is obscured. While the Catheter tip is wedged in small airways, bubbles may form that can obscure vision and lead to procedure delay.

notes.id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)::warning_49
notes.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
notes.text: If friction is felt in the trackball or scroll wheel, clean it with saline and dry with gauze prior to or during use, as needed.

notes.doc_id: Ion Endoluminal System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual(553990-11)
notes.text: Calibration initiates after installing the trackball and scroll wheel. Do not touch the trackball or scroll wheel during calibration.

setup_steps.text: Collect materials and prepare them for use.
Remove the Catheter Reprocessing Cover from the Catheter:
Inspect the Catheter Reprocessing Cover for any fluid, especially in the well that protects the green sensor port.
If not already done, move the System Cart to the desired location and apply the brakes.
Follow instructions in Chapter 5 Room Setup on page 48.
Position the patient on the procedure table (bed).

Intubate the patient with ET tube. Confirm that the distal end of the ET tube is approximately 2 to 5 cm proximal to the main carina. After the patient is intubated and under general anesthesia, secure the ET tube to the patient's head to prevent extubation.
Verify ET tube placement using a standard bronchoscope. Ensure minimal bends in the ET tube to facilitate smooth passage of the Catheter through the trachea.
Position the fluoro device to be used later in the procedure.
Connect the Swivel Connector to the ET tube after patient intubation.
Connect the anesthesia tubes to the Swivel Connector.

procedure_steps.text: Needle stroke length markings
If not already done, move the System Cart to the desired location and apply the brakes.
Follow instructions in Chapter 5 Room Setup on page 48.
Position the patient on the procedure table (bed).
Administer anesthesia.

Intubate the patient with ET tube. Confirm that the distal end of the ET tube is approximately 2 to 5 cm proximal to the main carina. After the patient is intubated and under general anesthesia, secure the ET tube to the patient's head to prevent extubation.
Verify ET tube placement using a standard bronchoscope. Ensure minimal bends in the ET tube to facilitate smooth passage of the Catheter through the trachea.
Position the fluoro device to be used later in the procedure.
Connect the Swivel Connector to the ET tube after patient intubation.
Connect the anesthesia tubes to the Swivel Connector.
Dock the arm to the Swivel Connector.
Use the Controller to drive the Catheter through the planned pathway to the target. Watch the Live View while driving.
Once the target is reached, note the message to use fluoroscopic guidance when extending tools past the tip of the Catheter.
(Optional) Perform a radial endobronchial ultrasound (R-EBUS) using fluoroscopy to confirm the target location.
Position the Catheter for biopsy.
Remove the Vision Probe from the Catheter and keep the Vision Probe out of the way by placing it into the Vision Probe bag.
For biopsy, adjust the fluoroscope to match the optimal fluoro angle on the top monitor.
Inspect the biopsy needle prior to use. If damaged, dispose and replace the needle.
Insert the biopsy needle through the Catheter tool channel. Secure the needle to the Catheter.

Under fluoroscopy, position the sheath for biopsy. Position the sheath so that it extends slightly beyond the Catheter, by loosening the thumbscrew on the needle handle. Approximately ¼ (one-fourth) turn of the thumbscrew allows the sheath to move back and forth.
While stabilizing the needle handle, set the needle insertion depth using the needle stop up to 3 cm based on the distance to the target and size of the target.
Under fluoroscopy, insert the needle with one jab towards the target.
Once the needle is inserted, remove the stylet from the back end of the needle while holding the needle in place.
Perform multiple jabs with the needle, per physician discretion.
Remove the vacuum syringe and, under fluoroscopy, fully retract the needle into the sheath, and return the needle stop to the home position.

If desired, fully retract the sheath and tighten the thumbscrew. If you opt to keep the sheath extended for further passes, exercise caution when re-inserting the needle into the Catheter tool channel.
Press the connector key and pull the biopsy needle from the Catheter tool channel.
Evaluate airway.
To repeat biopsy, insert the needle and repeat the needle biopsy steps to perform another biopsy pass from the same target to collect an appropriate sample size, at the physician's discretion.
Perform biopsy passes.
Remove samples from the needle (see Remove Samples on page 82).
Navigate to a second target (if applicable).
Repeat Navigation and Biopsy steps of the procedure.
If a biopsy tool (for example, needle, forceps, or brush) is advanced through the Catheter tool channel, retract the biopsy tool into its protective sheath and remove it from the Catheter.

Keep the Catheter attached to the arm (the Catheter shaft may remain inside the patient). If the Catheter is removed from the arm, you will need to complete Guided Setup and re-register after the system restarts.
Keep the system docked to the patient. If the system is undocked, you will need to complete Guided Setup and re-register after the system restarts.

If available, tap Restart System on the Controller touchscreen followed by Restart System . Alternatively, you can restart the system manually with the System Cart Power button (press and hold the Power button for three seconds to power off the system; when the system is powered off, press the button again to power the system back on).
When the system powers back on, tap Start Catheter Check if available on the Controller touchscreen.
After the Catheter check completes, compare Live View and Navigation View to assess registration.
If a biopsy tool (for example, needle, forceps, or brush) is advanced into tissue through the Catheter tool channel, retract the biopsy tool into its protective sheath and then into the Catheter.
Retract the Catheter using scroll wheel or carriage clutch button.
Retract the Catheter Guide and remove the Catheter from the ET tube.
Use the arm clutch button with one hand, and gently pull the Swivel Connector with the other hand to undock the arm and move it out of the way.
Adjust System Cart or bed height as needed.
Once adjustments are made, re-dock the system, insert the lubricated Catheter back into the ET tube, extend the Catheter Guide, and advance the Catheter.
Perform registration again.
If a biopsy tool (for example, needle, forceps, or brush) is advanced through the Catheter tool channel, retract the biopsy tool into its protective sheath and then remove it from the Catheter.
Retract the Catheter into the ET tube using the scroll wheel or carriage clutch button.
Retract the Catheter Guide.
Pull the Catheter out of the ET tube to remove the Catheter from the patient.
Remove Vision Probe from the Catheter, but keep it connected to the arm.
Disconnect the Catheter from the arm.
Tap Continue Procedure on the Controller touchscreen.
Raise the arm carriage, if needed.
Get a new Catheter, and then clean the sensor connections on the new Catheter and on the arm carriage using the Sensor Connection Cleaner (see Step 2 on page 60 and Step 3 on page 61).
Install the new Catheter and allow the Catheter self-tests to complete.
Insert the Vision Probe into the Catheter tool channel.
Lubricate the Catheter, and insert the Catheter into the ET tube.
Extend the Catheter Guide, and advance the Catheter.
Perform registration.

compatible_accessories: The use of third-party tools is at the discretion of the hospital and the physician.
Note:
Check compatibility of third-party tools prior to use.
Note:
Use only compatible bronchoscopic biopsy forceps.
Third-party tools must be legally marketed. Use the table below for guidance to select third-party tools.
Note: Third-party biopsy tools must be compatible with a 2 mm tool channel and have a minimum length of 100 cm.
For additional third-party product information, see Appendix C Third-Party Compatibility on page 106.
For third-party tool selection guidance, see 8.2 Select Compatible Third-Party Biopsy Tools on page 58.
Note: Do not advance forceps through the Catheter tool channel if the bend radius is smaller than 25 mm. Do not advance any other third-party tools if the bend radius is smaller than 20 mm.
Note: The rotational orientation of third-party tools is not controlled through the Catheter tool channel. Rotation may affect insertion and retraction through the Catheter.
1. Insert compatible third-party tools through the Catheter tool channel.
a. Ensure that the Catheter bend radius is greater than 25 mm if inserting forceps or greater than 20 mm if inserting any other third-party tools.
b. Once the device is inserted, the Catheter can be articulated to achieve a tighter bend radius, if needed.
2. Deploy the tool to retrieve the sample of the target tissue under fluoroscopy.
3. Remove the tool and evaluate the airway. Insert the Vision Probe into the Catheter to evaluate the biopsy site for bleeding.
Note: When possible before performing lavage, it is recommended to retract the Catheter so it is away from the airway walls for free fluid flow.
1. Connect the tubing of the bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) container to the narrowed, ribbed portion of the Suction Adapter.
2. Connect the wall suction tubing to the BAL container.
3. Infuse saline with a 20 mL syringe through the Catheter tool channel into the airways.
4. Connect the Suction Adapter, with the BAL container attached, onto the Catheter tool channel.
CAUTION: Do not apply suction for extended durations, as this may impair ventilation or lead to procedure delay.

5. To collect sample into BAL container, apply gentle suction by closing the hole on the suction adapter. Modulate suction strength by partially closing the hole on the suction adapter, or by varying pressure.
6. Disconnect the BAL container from the Catheter and remove from wall suction once sample has been retrieved.
1. Navigate to the target.
2. Load a compatible fiducial marker onto a compatible brush. The marker should be small enough to fit into the brush sheath, and large enough to fit snug between the sheath and the brush tip.
3. Plug the sheath tip with legally marketed bone wax. This will secure the fiducial marker for deployment.
4. Insert the brush through the Catheter.
5. Using fluoroscopic visualization, push out the fiducial marker from the sheath using the brush tip, and confirm deployment.
6. Remove the brush from the Catheter.
Contact your Intuitive representative for all validated third-party products.
The following third-party products may be referenced in this manual. All third-party products must be legally marketed.
Note: Use only water-based or silicone-based lubricants for the Catheter. Other lubricants may be difficult to remove during reprocessing and reduce the effectiveness of disinfection.

The Ion System with OnSite has been tested and found to be in compliance with IEC 60601-1-2, International standard for Medical electrical equipment - Part 1-2: General requirements for basic safety and essential performance - Collateral standard: Electromagnetic compatibility Requirements and tests. It is intended to be used in a procedure room environment and operation of the system is unaffected when used in the electromagnetic environment as specified in Tables 13 in this section. Special precautions and installation information for the system for Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) are provided in this section, see EMC Tables on page 111.

The performance of the system is unaffected when exposed to the electromagnetic environment as described in the IEC 60601-1-2 standard. There is no degradation of performance and therefore no risks to the patient or other devices due to Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) when used in the electromagnetic environment as specified in the tables in this section.
